newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU seeks WTO talks over Brazil car tariffs.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks WTO talks over Brazil car tariffs.

text.p: The European Union has started a case in the World Trade Organisation (WTO) against Brazil's tariff system for imported cars which Brussels says violate open trading rules, trade diplomats said on Tuesday.

They said the EU had notified the WTO that it was seeking consultations on the tariffs with Brazil under the trade body's dispute settlement system -- the first step towards the creation of a neutral panel.

Brazil is already in consultations with both Japan and the United States over the tariffs -- which set a rate of 35 percent for cars imported by manufacturers who also produce them in Brazil against 70 percent for other vehicles.
South Korea, which says its sales to Brazil have also been affected, has linked itself to the Japanese complaint.
EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan visited Brazil last month and held talks with government officials on the problem. He said afterwards he was not satisfied with what they had offered.

Under the WTO's dispute system, Brazil has 10 days to reply to the EU request and must begin talks within 30 days. If no settlement has been reached after 60 days, the EU can ask for a panel to be created.
